subject: botany_2
question_text: What are the physical factors responsible for the ascent of sap through xylem in plants?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.39, printed question 54. insider_note: Three named factors for two marks, so every name counts. Write the name first and the one-line meaning after it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Cohesion and adhesion
steps.margin_note: Both names with a one-line meaning each. Four lines.
lines: 2. Adhesion: the attraction of water molecules
TO the surface of the tracheal elements.
steps.why: Both are attractions, and naming what each attracts to what is the only way to keep them apart in an answer this short.
common_mistakes: Swapping them. Cohesion is water to water; adhesion is water to the wall.
Writing the names with no meaning. The one-line meaning is what earns the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Cohesion: water to water. Adhesion: water to wall.

steps.label: Transpiration pull
steps.margin_note: Name the third factor and say it is the driving force.

lines.text: Two attractions hold the column, one pull moves it

lines: 3. Transpiration pull: the driving force for
the upward movement of water, created when
steps.why: Cohesion and adhesion only hold the column together; transpiration pull is the one factor that actually supplies force, so it is named last and separately.
common_mistakes: Naming only one attraction. Cohesion and adhesion are both needed, and transpiration pull is the driving force.
Calling transpiration pull a push. It is a PULL from the leaf end.
